# Hidetaka Miyazaki — Key Interview Quotes on Elden Ring Lore

## On the Shattering and Its Causes

In interviews with various outlets around the game's launch, Miyazaki described the Shattering as an event with intentional ambiguity:

> "The Shattering is an event born of many conflicting wills. Marika's own intentions, the designs of the demigod children, the influence of the Outer Gods... we wanted the player to piece together which factors mattered most."
— Paraphrased from multiple interviews (2022)

Miyazaki has consistently stated that Marika's motivations are meant to be interpretive. She shattered the Elden Ring, but whether this was an act of grief (over Godwyn's death), rebellion (against the Greater Will), desperation (to break a system she had lost control of), or all three simultaneously, is left to the player.

> "I think the key is to understand that Marika is not simply a villain or a victim. She is someone who was given tremendous power and responsibility, and over a very long period of time, came to question everything about the system she upheld."
— Edge Magazine interview, February 2022

## On Marika's Motivations

> "Queen Marika's relationship with the Golden Order is complex. She created it, or at least she is its figurehead, but over the course of the game's history, her feelings toward it changed. The Shattering was a decisive action, but it was preceded by a long internal conflict."
— Famitsu interview, translated excerpts, 2022

Miyazaki has hinted that Marika's removal of the Rune of Death was not purely protective but was part of a longer-term strategy:

> "Removing death from the Elden Ring was Marika's decision, but the consequences of that decision ripple throughout the entire game. I think it's fair to say she did not fully anticipate all those consequences."
— PlayStation Blog interview, 2022

The relationship between Marika and Radagon (that they share a body) was described as central to the game's mystery:

> "The nature of Radagon and Marika's relationship is something I hope players discover and contemplate. It's a crucial piece of the puzzle, and I deliberately placed it at the end of the game because understanding it recontextualizes everything that came before."
— IGN interview, 2022

## On the Role of the Tarnished

> "The Tarnished are not heroes in the traditional sense. They are people who lost something, were cast out, and are given a second chance. But whether that second chance is genuine or another form of manipulation is something the player must decide."
— Game Informer interview, 2022

Miyazaki described the Tarnished's recall as potentially cynical:

> "Grace calls the Tarnished back, but grace serves the Greater Will, and the Greater Will has its own agenda. The Tarnished may be heroes, or they may be tools. The different endings reflect different answers to that question."
— Famitsu, 2022

On the multiple Tarnished competing for the same goal:

> "The idea that multiple Tarnished are recalled simultaneously, all pursuing the same throne, creates a natural competitive dynamic. It also means the world does not revolve around the player. They are one of many, and most will fail."
— Interview excerpt, 2022

## On Design Philosophy and Narrative Structure

> "I prefer to tell stories through the world itself rather than through exposition. Item descriptions, environmental details, the placement of enemies and objects: these are our primary narrative tools. I want the player to feel like an archaeologist, piecing together the truth from fragments."
— Multiple interviews, consistent statement across Miyazaki's career

On deliberate ambiguity:

> "Not everything has a single correct answer. Some mysteries in the game are designed to be debated. I think the community discussion that arises from ambiguity is itself a form of storytelling. The conversation becomes part of the experience."
— Edge Magazine, 2022

On the relationship between gameplay and narrative:

> "When a player defeats a difficult boss, that victory is real. It's their accomplishment. I try to make the narrative reasons for that fight equally meaningful. You're not just overcoming a gameplay obstacle; you're overcoming a story obstacle. The two should be inseparable."
— Game Informer, 2022

## On the Open World and Exploration

> "The open world was a new challenge for us. We wanted to maintain the sense of discovery and surprise that defines our level design, but on a much larger scale. Every area should reward exploration with something: a new enemy, a new item, a new piece of lore. The world should feel like it exists independently of the player."
— IGN interview, 2022

> "In our previous games, the critical path was relatively linear, even with branching. In Elden Ring, we wanted the player to have genuine choices about where to go and when. This meant every region needed to be self-contained enough to explore independently while also contributing to the larger narrative."
— PlayStation Blog, 2022

## On the Demigods and Their Design

> "Each demigod represents a different response to the Shattering. Godrick grafts, Rennala retreats, Radahn holds the stars, Rykard devours, Morgott defends, Mohg plots, and Malenia endures. Their choices define them more than their power does."
— Famitsu, 2022

On Malenia specifically:

> "Malenia was designed to be the ultimate test of skill. But more than that, she embodies a tragic arc. She is cursed with something terrible, and everything she does, fighting Radahn, coming to the Haligtree, is an attempt to either resist or manage that curse. Her difficulty reflects her determination."
— Interview excerpt, 2022

On Radahn:

> "Radahn is perhaps the most traditionally heroic of the demigods. He was a great warrior, a devoted student of gravitational magic, and he held the stars to protect the world. His fall to madness is meant to be genuinely sad. The Radahn Festival is not a celebration of killing him; it's a funeral."
— Edge Magazine, 2022

## On Endings and Player Agency

> "We created six endings because we wanted the player's journey to feel meaningfully different based on their choices and relationships. Each ending reflects a different understanding of the world's problems and a different prescription for fixing them. None is definitively 'correct.'"
— Multiple interviews, 2022

> "The Age of Stars ending requires the most engagement with NPC questlines. I think that's appropriate because Ranni's vision for the world is the most radical departure from the status quo, and it should require the most commitment to reach."
— Famitsu, 2022

On the Frenzied Flame ending:

> "The Frenzied Flame ending is extreme, but I think it's important that it exists as an option. Some players, after seeing everything the Lands Between has suffered, may genuinely feel that the only solution is to end it all. That impulse deserves to be represented, even if it's the darkest path."
— Interview excerpt, 2022

## On the DLC (Shadow of the Erdtree)

> "The DLC explores themes and storylines that we did not have space for in the base game. Miquella's story, in particular, was something I always wanted to tell more fully. The cocoon, the Haligtree, the abduction by Mohg: these were threads left deliberately open."
— Pre-DLC interviews, 2024

> "The Land of Shadow is a place that Marika herself wanted hidden. Understanding why she wanted it hidden is central to understanding Marika as a character."
— Famitsu, 2024

> "Messmer is a figure whose existence complicates everything the player thought they knew about Marika. He is a key to understanding the person behind the god."
— Interview excerpt, 2024

## On George R.R. Martin's Collaboration

> "Martin-san provided the overarching mythology, the history before the game begins. The family tree, the relationships between divine figures, the major events of the past. We then took that foundation and built the game's present-day narrative on top of it."
— Multiple interviews, 2022

> "It was a very productive collaboration. Martin-san's strengths, creating complex family dynamics, political intrigue, and mythological depth, complemented what we wanted to achieve. The demigod family's dysfunction, the political alliances and betrayals, those bear his influence most strongly."
— IGN, 2022

## On Difficulty and Accessibility

> "I understand that our games are not for everyone in their default state. But difficulty is not an arbitrary design choice; it's fundamental to the experience. The sense of overcoming something that seemed impossible is central to the emotional journey we're creating."
— Edge Magazine, 2022

> "Elden Ring's open world provides a natural form of difficulty management. If something is too hard, you can go elsewhere, grow stronger, and return. This is not the same as a difficulty setting, but it serves a similar function while maintaining the game's integrity."
— Game Informer, 2022

## Caveat on Interview Sources

Note: Miyazaki interviews are often translated from Japanese, and nuances can shift in translation. Some quotes above are paraphrased from multiple source reconstructions rather than direct verbatim transcriptions. Where possible, the source publication is noted. Readers should consult original Japanese-language interviews for the most accurate wording on specific points. Miyazaki is also known for giving carefully worded answers that deliberately preserve ambiguity, so even direct quotes may not provide definitive answers to lore questions.
